Magnetic relaxation

Words: 237 Articles: 4
Ideal magnetohydrodynamics OurBigBook.com
Magnetic relaxation converts magnetic energy into material motion through the Lorentz force density, and dissipates the resulting kinetic energy through viscosity. In a perfect conductor, magnetic flux freezing preserves field-line connectivity throughout every smooth stage. A regular limiting state has zero velocity and is a magnetostatic equilibrium, but its magnetic field can contain current sheets. Conservation of one global magnetic helicity is weaker than preservation of the complete frozen field-line structure.

Single-molecule magnet

Words: 26
Magnetic relaxation OurBigBook.com
A finite molecular spin system exhibiting slow reversal of its magnetic moment on an experimental timescale. Blocking is timescale-dependent and does not require bulk long-range magnetic order.

Quantum tunnelling of magnetization

Words: 17
Magnetic relaxation OurBigBook.com
Reversal between opposite magnetic orientations through quantum mixing rather than activation over the full classical anisotropy barrier.

Collapse of a planar magnetic separatrix

Words: 74
Magnetic relaxation OurBigBook.com
For a planar magnetic field B=(ψy​,−ψx​,0), ideal induction advects the Cartesian magnetic flux function: Dt​ψ=0. Incompressible flow also preserves the area inside each material contour. During relaxation, the arms of a magnetic separatrix can approach each other while their field-line connectivity remains fixed. A transition of width ϵ with a finite change of tangential field has electric current density of order ϵ−1 and can approach a current sheet. This is a possible limiting mechanism, not a claim that every planar equilibrium is singular.

Viscous magnetic-relaxation energy identity (E˙=−ρν∫D​∣∇×v∣2dV)

Words: 66
Magnetic relaxation OurBigBook.com
For constant mass density ρ, kinematic viscosity ν>0, ideal induction, zero boundary velocity and tangent magnetic field, put E=∫D​[ρ∣v∣2/2+∣B∣2/(2μ0​)]dV. Multiplying the momentum equation by v and integrating cancels pressure work and advective flux. The magnetic-energy derivative is minus the integral of Lorentz force density dotted with velocity, canceling the same work in the kinetic-energy equation. Integration by parts then gives the displayed identity. For incompressible flow with zero boundary velocity, ∫∣∇v∣2=∫∣∇×v∣2.

Steady planar ideal-MHD field-line invariants (u=kB/ρ+Uez​)

Words: 154 Articles: 2
Ideal magnetohydrodynamics OurBigBook.com
For a stationary, z-independent ideal magnetohydrodynamics flow with Ez​=0, nonzero horizontal magnetic field and nonzero magnetohydrodynamic mass loading k, the displayed decomposition has B⋅∇k=B⋅∇U=0. The continuity equation gives the first invariant, and the ideal magnetohydrodynamic induction equation gives the second. Entropy and V=uz​−Bz​/(μ0​k) are also constant on each magnetic field line. Stationarity alone permits constant nonzero Ez​, so it does not imply this decomposition.

Steady planar ideal-MHD field-line invariants OurBigBook.com
The two axial invariants in steady planar ideal-MHD field-line invariants give the displayed identity. When V−U=0, a finite smooth flow cannot reach horizontal Alfvén speed. When V=U, an everywhere Alfvénic branch is possible even with Bz​=0: constant ρ and u=B/μ0​ρ​ give an example. The nondegenerate exclusion must not be applied to this branch.

The horizontal total energy flux, including the Poynting vector, is kBh​Q. The magnetic correction accounts for work exchanged between the fluid and the field.

Reduced magnetohydrodynamics (k∥​/k⊥​≪1)

Words: 262 Articles: 2
Ideal magnetohydrodynamics OurBigBook.com
Reduced magnetohydrodynamics is the leading ideal-fluid description of small, anisotropic fluctuations about a strong uniform guide field, with k∥​/k⊥​∼δB⊥​/B0​∼δu⊥​/vA​≪1. Its solenoidal perpendicular Elsässer variables obey
∂t​z⊥±​∓vA​∂z​z⊥±​+(z⊥∓​⋅∇⊥​)z⊥±​=−∇⊥​Π.
(2)
The parallel magnetic derivative includes bending of field lines: ∇∥​=∂z​+(δB⊥​/B0​)⋅∇⊥​. Slow compressive and entropy mode fluctuations are passively transported at this order. The system excludes the rapidly propagating fast magnetosonic wave sector rather than describing all possible MHD perturbations.

Five quadratic cascade invariants of anisotropic magnetohydrodynamic turbulence (IA+​,IA−​,IS+​,IS−​,Ie​)

Words: 118
Reduced magnetohydrodynamics OurBigBook.com
For ideal reduced magnetohydrodynamics with periodic or vanishing-flux boundaries, the five quadratic cascade channels are IA±​=∫∣z⊥±​∣2dV, IS±​=∫(f±)2dV and Ie​=∫s2dV. The perpendicular Elsässer variables, slow-wave amplitudes f±, and entropy fluctuation s each obey an equation with divergence-free advection. Multiplying each equation by its own field and integrating makes both advection and propagation terms boundary fluxes, while the perpendicular pressure term vanishes by solenoidality. Each integral is therefore separately conserved. The two Alfvén cascades distort one another without exchanging their integrated invariants; the other three are passively cascaded by the Alfvénic motion without feedback at this order. This count concerns quadratic fluctuation-energy channels: an advected scalar also conserves arbitrary integrals ∫F(s)dV, which are not extra independent quadratic modal channels.

Slow and entropy fluctuations in reduced magnetohydrodynamics (Df±=∓cT​∇∥​f±)

Words: 80
Reduced magnetohydrodynamics OurBigBook.com
In ideal reduced magnetohydrodynamics with constant background sound and Alfvén speeds, perpendicular total-pressure balance gives δp+ρ0​vA2​δB∥​/B0​=0. Put s=δp/p0​−γδρ/ρ0​, r=δρ/ρ0​+s/γ, cT​=vA​cs​/(vA2​+cs2​)1/2 and h=cs2​r/cT​. Then the parallel momentum, continuity and induction equations yield
Du∥​=−cT​∇∥​h,Dh=−cT​∇∥​u∥​,Ds=0.
(3)
Thus f±=u∥​±h satisfy Df±=∓cT​∇∥​f±. The two slow-wave populations propagate along bent magnetic field lines and are mixed by the perpendicular Alfvénic turbulence, while the entropy fluctuation is simply advected. They do not force the perpendicular Alfvénic system at this leading order.

Ideal magnetohydrodynamic energy conservation (∂t​E+∇⋅F=0)

Words: 52
Ideal magnetohydrodynamics OurBigBook.com
For a fixed Newtonian gravitational potential, total energy density is E=ρ(u2/2+Φ)+p/(γ−1)+B2/(2μ0​). Its flux combines advected kinetic/potential energy, specific enthalpy and the Poynting vector. Dotting the ideal magnetohydrodynamic momentum equation with velocity, adding the adiabatic internal energy equation and the magnetic energy equation cancels the magnetic work. The pressure terms combine into −∇⋅(pu), proving the conservation law. A time-dependent imposed potential instead contributes ρ∂t​Φ.

Ideal magnetohydrodynamic momentum equation (ρDt​u=−∇p−ρ∇Φ+(∇×B)×B/μ0​)

Words: 22
Ideal magnetohydrodynamics OurBigBook.com
The inviscid magnetohydrodynamic momentum equation balances inertia, pressure, gravitational acceleration and Lorentz force density. The magnetic force separates into magnetic tension and magnetic pressure. It is coupled to the continuity equation and the ideal magnetohydrodynamic induction equation.

Ideal magnetohydrodynamics OurBigBook.com
A useful ideal magnetohydrodynamics reduction has u=v(z,t)+axey​, B=B(z,t) and ρ=ρ(z,t). The constant background shear flow supplies avx​ in the axial momentum equation and aBx​ in axial magnetic induction. The solenoidal constraint and MHD induction equation together make Bz​ constant.

Words: 38
Plane-parallel magnetohydrodynamic flow with imposed shear OurBigBook.com
At w2=vaz2​, the transverse steady equations require wBx​w′=0 and wBy​w′=a(wBx​−Bz​vx​). These conditions can be lost by division when eliminating transverse magnetic derivatives. A scalar equation displaying the magnetosonic critical speeds need not display every compatibility condition at an Alfvén speed.

Magnetohydrodynamic shear work (S=a(Bx​By​/μ0​−ρvx​vy​))

Words: 38
Plane-parallel magnetohydrodynamic flow with imposed shear OurBigBook.com
The energy of the residual flow and magnetic field in a maintained shear flow has source S=−aTxy​, where Txy​=ρvx​vy​−Bx​By​/μ0​. The kinetic and magnetic stresses can exchange energy with the imposed background. The source vanishes when their off-diagonal contributions cancel.

Ideal magnetohydrodynamic equations (∂t​U+Ai​(U)∂i​U=0)

Words: 31
Ideal magnetohydrodynamics OurBigBook.com
The smooth ideal-MHD system couples mass conservation, momentum, adiabatic pressure transport and the ideal magnetohydrodynamic induction equation, subject to the solenoidal magnetic-field constraint. Without gravity it is a quasilinear partial differential equation system. Across shocks, conservative total energy replaces smooth adiabatic pressure transport.

Magnetohydrodynamic energy principle

Words: 285 Articles: 3
Ideal magnetohydrodynamics OurBigBook.com
For a static smooth ideal magnetohydrodynamics equilibrium with conservative external forces and surface terms eliminated by the boundary conditions, the linear displacement equation is ρξ¨​=Fξ, where the force operator is a self-adjoint operator in the appropriate integral pairing. Its restoring quadratic form δW=−21​∫ξ∗⋅FξdV is real. Multiplying the normal mode equation by the complex conjugate of the displacement and integrating gives ω2∫ρ∣ξ∣2dV=2δW. Hence squared frequencies are real, and a negative restoring form gives an unstable mode through the variational Rayleigh quotient, subject to the operator domain and spectral hypotheses. Background fluid flow adds terms to this argument; the static hypothesis is essential.

Incompressible magnetic displacement energy identity (σ2∫ρ∣ξ∣2=∫ξi∗​ξj​(Π,ij​+ρΦ,ij​)+μ0−1​∫∣(B⋅∇)ξ∣2)

Words: 138 Articles: 1
Magnetohydrodynamic energy principle OurBigBook.com
For a static ideal magnetohydrodynamics equilibrium in fixed gravity, let ∇⋅ξ=0 and Π=p+B2/(2μ0​). Frozen flux gives b=(B⋅∇)ξ−(ξ⋅∇)B and continuity gives ρ′=−ξ⋅∇ρ. Multiplying the linear momentum equation by the conjugate displacement and integrating by parts gives the displayed identity when surface terms vanish. The two magnetic cross terms cancel; the remaining magnetic equilibrium derivative combines with the mass density-gradient force to give the two Hessian matrices. Real symmetric Hessian matrices and the nonnegative magnetic tension term make σ2 real.

Interchange stability of an incompressible magnetized atmosphere (Q=−g∫ρz​∣ξz​∣2+μ0−1​∫B2∣∂x​ξ∣2)

Words: 66
Incompressible magnetic displacement energy identity OurBigBook.com
For a horizontal field B(z)ex​ in constant downward gravity, equilibrium obeys (p+B2/(2μ0​))z​=−ρg. The displacement energy reduces to the displayed quadratic form. Perturbations independent of the field direction do not bend magnetic field lines and therefore have no magnetic tension penalty: an increasing mass density with height permits instability. A nonincreasing mass density gives nonnegative energy for all admitted incompressible perturbations. Along-field variation adds magnetic tension proportional to wavenumber squared, stabilizing sufficiently short waves when buoyancy is unfavorable.

Linear displacement equations for a magnetized atmosphere (δρ=−∇⋅(ρξ),δB=∇×(ξ×B))

Words: 55
Magnetohydrodynamic energy principle OurBigBook.com
For a static equilibrium and a fluid Lagrangian displacement ξ, conservation of mass, adiabatic entropy and magnetic flux freezing give δp=−ξ⋅∇p−γp∇⋅ξ together with the displayed relations. Linearizing the pressure/tension form of the momentum equation yields ρξ¨​=−∇δΠ−gδρez​+μ0−1​(δB⋅∇B+B⋅∇δB), where δΠ=δp+B⋅δB/μ0​. Static force balance removes the zeroth-order terms; the density multiplying acceleration is the equilibrium density.

Elsässer variable (z±)

Words: 112 Articles: 1
Ideal magnetohydrodynamics OurBigBook.com
For an incompressible flow with constant mass density, the Elsässer variables are z±=u±va​, where va​ is the Alfvén velocity. Adding and subtracting the Euler momentum equation and ideal magnetohydrodynamic induction equation yields ∂t​z±+(z∓⋅∇)z±=−∇ψ, with ψ=p/ρ+Φ+∣va​∣2/2 and ∇⋅z±=0. Thus each field is transported by the other, a useful way to expose interactions of oppositely directed Alfvén waves.

Elsässer energy invariant (I±​)

Words: 58
Elsässer variable OurBigBook.com
For smooth ideal magnetohydrodynamics of constant mass density, define I±​=∫V​∣z±∣2dV. Taking the dot product of the Elsässer variable equation with 2z± gives
∂t​∣z±∣2+∇⋅(∣z±∣2z∓+2ψz±)=0.
(4)
Therefore each integral is constant when its outward boundary flux vanishes, for example when both velocity and magnetic field are tangent to the fixed boundary, or for periodic boundary conditions. The kinetic energy plus magnetic energy is ρ(I+​+I−​)/4, while the cross-helicity is μ0​ρ​(I+​−I−​)/4.

Cross-helicity (Hc​=∫u⋅BdV)

Words: 194 Articles: 2
Ideal magnetohydrodynamics OurBigBook.com
Cross-helicity measures alignment between velocity and magnetic field in a magnetized fluid. Its density is hc​=u⋅B.

Cross-helicity conservation law

Words: 175 Articles: 1
Cross-helicity OurBigBook.com
Let hc​=u⋅B be the cross-helicity density. The ideal magnetohydrodynamic induction equation implies DB/Dt=(B⋅∇)u−B∇⋅u. Dotting the momentum equation with B eliminates the Lorentz force density, since it is perpendicular to the magnetic field. The material derivative of hc​ is therefore
DtDhc​​=B⋅∇(2u2​−Φ)−ρB⋅∇p​−hc​∇⋅u.
(5)
Using dh=Tds+dp/ρ for specific enthalpy h and specific entropy s, together with Gauss's law for magnetism, converts this to
∂t​hc​+∇⋅[uhc​+B(h+Φ−2u2​)]=TB⋅∇s.
(6)
The source vanishes when magnetic field lines lie in constant-specific entropy surfaces, in particular in a homentropic flow. Integrating over a volume conserves its total cross-helicity only if the boundary flux also vanishes. This local law is derived in Ogilvie's astrophysical fluid dynamics notes.

Material conservation of cross-helicity density

Words: 68
Cross-helicity conservation law OurBigBook.com
In a homentropic flow, the cross-helicity conservation law gives
DtDhc​​=B⋅∇(2u2​−h−Φ)−hc​∇⋅u.
(7)
Consequently cross-helicity density is conserved along each trajectory exactly when the right-hand side vanishes. In a steady state, mass conservation gives ∇⋅u=−u⋅∇logρ, so the criterion becomes
B⋅∇(h+Φ−2u2​)=(u⋅B)u⋅∇logρ.
(8)
The absence of an entropy source in a conservation law does not alone make its density an advected scalar: compression and transport along the magnetic field still change that density.

Magnetic flux freezing

Words: 188 Articles: 4
Ideal magnetohydrodynamics OurBigBook.com
Magnetic flux freezing states that every material loop in an ideal conducting fluid encloses constant magnetic flux. A deformation perpendicular to a uniform field that preserves mass per unit length therefore preserves B/ρ.

Material magnetic-flux transport theorem (dΦB​/dt=∫S(t)​[∂t​B−∇×(u×B)+u∇⋅B]⋅dS)

Words: 46
Magnetic flux freezing OurBigBook.com
Combine the material surface element evolution law with the product rule for B⋅dS. The result is
dtd​∫S(t)​B⋅dS=∫S(t)​[DtDB​+B∇⋅u−(B⋅∇)u]⋅dS.
(9)
Expanding the curl gives the equivalent title formula. The ideal magnetohydrodynamic induction equation and Gauss's law for magnetism make the integrand zero and prove magnetic flux freezing, without requiring incompressible flow.

Flux-surface preservation during magnetic-tube expansion

Words: 46
Magnetic flux freezing OurBigBook.com
Suppose the Cartesian magnetic flux function is advected, the initial axial velocity is zero, By​=f(ψ) initially, and ∇⋅u=g(ψ,t). Then By​=f(ψ)exp[−∫0t​g(ψ,s)ds] remains a function of the flux label and time. The axial Lorentz force vanishes because its transverse derivative along a magnetic field line vanishes. Smooth ideal evolution therefore preserves zero axial motion.

Words: 62 Articles: 1
Magnetic flux freezing OurBigBook.com
The mass-to-flux ratio is the matter carried per unit magnetic flux by a bundle of field lines. Ideal magnetohydrodynamics preserves it for a material flux tube.

Critical mass-to-flux ratio ((M/Φ)crit​=λ/μ0​G​)

Words: 36
Mass-to-flux ratio OurBigBook.com
For fixed cloud shape, gravitational energy scales as −Cg​GM2/L and magnetic energy as CB​Φ2/(μ0​L). The magnetic-criticality threshold for negligible pressure is M/Φ>CB​/Cg​​/μ0​G​. Ideal flux freezing keeps this ratio fixed during homologous collapse; geometry determines the numerical coefficient.

The Alfvén speed associated with magnetic-field magnitude B and density ρ is vA​=B/μ0​ρ​.

Alfvén Mach number (MA​=u/vA​)

Words: 66
Alfvén speed OurBigBook.com
The Alfvén Mach number compares a characteristic flow speed with the Alfvén speed vA​=B/μ0​ρ​. In an axisymmetric magnetohydrodynamic wind, the relevant poloidal quantity is MAp​=∣up​∣μ0​ρ​/∣Bp​∣. With magnetohydrodynamic mass loading ρup​=κBp​, its square is μ0​κ2/ρ. The Alfvén surface is the locus MAp​=1, and a smooth crossing requires the corresponding Alfvén-surface regularity condition for an axisymmetric wind. The total-speed and poloidal-speed definitions should be distinguished when there is substantial rotation or a strong toroidal magnetic field.

Alfvén velocity (va​)

Ambipolar damping is attenuation of magnetic disturbances by friction between the magnetically coupled charged fluid and a neutral fluid. In a strongly collisional mixture, the fluids nearly move together, but their small relative velocity dissipates energy. With drag coefficient ρi​μin​=ρn​μni​, the frictional energy loss is −ρi​μin​∫∣ui​−un​∣2dV. Neglecting other dissipative processes does not remove this collisional loss.

Alfvén wave

Words: 2k Articles: 19
Magnetohydrodynamic wave OurBigBook.com
An Alfvén wave is a magnetohydrodynamic wave in which magnetic tension restores a sideways disturbance of a conducting fluid. In the small-amplitude, uniform-background ideal magnetohydrodynamics model, its shear polarization of waves has displacement perpendicular to both the background magnetic field and the wavevector. It is an incompressible flow disturbance: the mass density and gas pressure have no first-order fluctuation. Its dispersion relation is ω2=(k⋅vA​)2, where vA​ is the background Alfvén velocity.
The mechanism resembles a plucked taut string: magnetic flux freezing makes sideways fluid flow bend magnetic field lines, and their magnetic tension accelerates neighboring fluid. The fluid supplies inertia and the bent magnetic field supplies the restoring stress. This permits energy transport without a first-order compression, unlike an acoustic wave. Hannes Alfvén's 1942 paper, Existence of Electromagnetic-Hydrodynamic Waves, considered precisely a uniform axial magnetic field, infinite electrical conductivity and sideways velocity depending on axial position and time; it proposed a solar application. This was a theoretical prediction, followed by the distinct Lundquist liquid-metal Alfvén wave experiment.[ref]
For oblique propagation, the shear Alfvén wave has velocity normal to the plane containing the wavevector and background magnetic field. The fast magnetosonic wave and slow magnetosonic wave instead have velocity in that plane and generally involve compression, with gas pressure and magnetic pressure contributing to their restoring forces. For exactly parallel propagation the plane is not unique: either transverse polarization of waves is allowed, and some modal speeds coincide. For k∥​=0 the shear branch has ω=0, while the fast magnetosonic wave can still propagate perpendicular to the magnetic field. One should identify the polarization of waves as well as the phase velocity. The statement that the shear mode is incompressible concerns this linear mode; a finite linearly polarized disturbance can drive a quadratic compressive response, as in the magnetic-pressure obstruction to a linearly polarized Alfvén wave.

Linear Alfvén wave equations (ω=±k∥​vA​)

Words: 234
Alfvén wave OurBigBook.com
Take a static uniform fluid of mass density ρ>0, constant gas pressure, and background magnetic field B0​=B0​ez​ with B0​>0. Use SI units, vacuum permeability μ0​, zero electrical resistivity and zero viscosity. Write B=B0​+b⊥​(z,t) and u=u⊥​(z,t), with both disturbances perpendicular to ez​. Retain only linear order in their amplitudes. There is no background fluid flow, so the linear material derivative is ∂t​.
The continuity equation has ∇⋅u⊥​=0, hence ∂t​δρ=0; choosing no initial mass density fluctuation gives δρ=0. For this shear mode the gas pressure fluctuation is also zero. In the ideal magnetohydrodynamic momentum equation, the Lorentz force density can be written
μ0​(∇×B)×B​=μ0​(B⋅∇)B​−∇2μ0​B2​.
(11)
Because B0​⋅b⊥​=0, the perturbed magnetic pressure starts at quadratic order. The surviving transverse magnetic tension gives the first equation below. Expanding the ideal magnetohydrodynamic induction equation gives the second:
ρ∂t​u⊥​=μ0​B0​​∂z​b⊥​,∂t​b⊥​=B0​∂z​u⊥​.
(12)
Differentiate the first in time and substitute the second. Both velocity and magnetic field disturbances obey the one-dimensional wave equation:
∂t2​u⊥​=vA2​∂z2​u⊥​,vA​=μ0​ρ​B0​​.
(13)
For a plane wave proportional to ei(k∥​z−ωt), this gives ω2=k∥2​vA2​, or ω=±k∥​vA​. The magnetic and velocity amplitudes satisfy b⊥​=−(B0​k∥​/ω)u⊥​: they have opposite signs for propagation along +ez​ and equal signs for propagation along −ez​. The general uniform-background shear polarization of waves, perpendicular to both k and B0​, gives the same dispersion relation with k∥​=k⋅ez​. Its group velocity is ±vA​ez​, whereas its phase velocity normal to an oblique wavefront has magnitude vA​∣k∥​∣/∣k∣.

Alfvén wave OurBigBook.com
Dot the two Linear Alfvén wave equations with u⊥​ and b⊥​/μ0​, respectively, and add. The result is conservation of energy with
E=2ρ∣u⊥​∣2​+2μ0​∣b⊥​∣2​,Fz​=−μ0​B0​​u⊥​⋅b⊥​.
(14)
A single traveling Alfvén wave has equal kinetic energy and perturbation magnetic energy, and Fz​=±vA​E. This equality need not hold instantaneously at each point of a superposed standing wave.
As an original ideal-model example, stipulate B0​=1.00T, ρ=104kgm−3 and a uniform path L=0.20m. Using μ0​≃4π×10−7Hm−1, the Alfvén speed is 8.92ms−1 and the transit time L/vA​ is 22.4ms. Doubling the magnetic field halves that time. A sinusoidal velocity with peak amplitude 0.010ms−1 has magnetic peak amplitude 1.12mT and mean energy flux ⟨Fz​⟩=ρvA​U2/2=4.46Wm−2 in the positive direction. These are stipulated ideal parameters, not historical measurements or a prediction including vessel walls.

Words: 175
Alfvén wave OurBigBook.com
Finite electrical conductivity σ allows magnetic diffusion, with magnetic diffusivity ηm​=1/(μ0​σ). In the same uniform, unbounded geometry as the Linear Alfvén wave equations, neglect viscosity but add ηm​∂z2​b⊥​ to induction. For real k∥​ and time dependence e−iωt, elimination gives

(15)
Thus weak magnetic diffusion, ηm​∣k∥​∣≪vA​, gives an amplitude decay rate ηm​k∥2​/2. For ηm​∣k∥​∣>2vA​, both temporal roots are purely decaying; they no longer describe an oscillating traveling mode. This temporal calculation at fixed real wavenumber is different from a driven vessel at fixed real frequency, where a complex spatial wavenumber describes penetration and attenuation. Viscosity also dissipates kinetic energy, and walls introduce transverse gradients and additional losses.
For an axial length L, comparing the magnetic diffusion time L2/ηm​ with the transit time L/vA​ gives the ratio LvA​/ηm​. A large value favors propagation before diffusion, but a narrow vessel can introduce a shorter transverse diffusion scale. In the actual 1949 analysis, finite electrical conductivity and vessel dimensions restrict the useful frequency interval; above its upper limit the response becomes a skin wave.[ref]

Lundquist liquid-metal Alfvén wave experiment (1949)

Words: 290
Alfvén wave OurBigBook.com
Stig Lundquist, the author printed as S. Lundquist, reported an early laboratory test in 1949. The apparatus used mercury in a stainless-steel cylinder, a vibrating disk, and a floating mirror to indicate the motion at the liquid surface. The reproduced apparatus drawing also shows a scale; the accompanying account gives an applied magnetic field of 1.3T.[ref]
The imposed magnetic field ran along the cylinder, while the bottom disk oscillated to excite azimuthal motion. Varying the drive frequency sought a standing wave resonance. A later authored experimental account describes this as an early hint: the resonance peak was not reached, and magnetic damping was substantial.[ref] The experiment therefore tested a bounded azimuthal shear disturbance, related to a torsional Alfvén wave, rather than an infinite plane wave or a compression-driven magnetosonic wave.
The magnetic field provides the controlled physical parameter: the ideal Alfvén wave prediction makes a propagation speed proportional to its strength, while a resonance also depends on the vessel's boundary conditions. A quantitative test must compare the driven response with finite-electrical conductivity theory and account for mechanical coupling and wall losses. An observed surface motion alone cannot distinguish all these mechanisms. The reproduced apparatus account gives neither a numerical drive frequency nor a field-off comparison. Lundquist's paper itself calls the experiment preliminary and proposes further investigations.[ref]

Its nonzero vorticity disproves the unrestricted zero-vorticity reduction. Exponentially growing modes with real background coefficients cannot encounter these real-frequency resonances.

A cylindrical force-free magnetic field depends only on cylindrical radius and has current everywhere parallel to its magnetic field. Regularity on the axis often forces its radial component to vanish.

Linearized ideal magnetohydrodynamic equations (linearized ideal MHD equations)

Words: 95 Articles: 1
Ideal magnetohydrodynamics OurBigBook.com
The linearized ideal magnetohydrodynamic equations retain terms first order in perturbations about a chosen ideal-MHD background. Around a uniform state they describe Alfvén waves and magnetosonic waves.

Displacement equation for a parallel magnetic shear flow ([(ρS2−kx2​B2)f′]′−k2(ρS2−kx2​B2)f=0)

Words: 71
Linearized ideal magnetohydrodynamic equations OurBigBook.com
For nonresonant incompressible normal modes of a uniform-density shear flow with aligned uniform magnetic field, let S=σ+kx​U(z), k2=kx2​+ky2​ and f=w/S. The normal displacement is f/i. The linearized horizontal equations and incompressibility give ik2p1​=ρ(Sw′−S′w)=ρS2f′. Substituting the ideal magnetohydrodynamic induction equation into normal momentum gives the displayed conservative equation. Across a zero-thickness shear layer, continuity of f and of (ρS2−kx2​B2)f′ supplies the interface conditions. They express common normal displacement and continuous perturbed magnetohydrodynamic total pressure, avoiding undefined products of distributional shear gradients.

Ideal magnetohydrodynamic induction equation (ideal MHD induction equation)

Words: 378 Articles: 7
Ideal magnetohydrodynamics OurBigBook.com
The ideal magnetohydrodynamic induction equation is ∂t​B=∇×(u×B). Together with ∇⋅B=0, it implies magnetic-flux freezing.

Ideal magnetic response to a cylindrical cyclonic event (A=B0​rsin(ϕ−ft),Bz​=B0​tg′cos(ϕ−ft))

Words: 79
Ideal magnetohydrodynamic induction equation OurBigBook.com
For an axisymmetric velocity u=(0,rf(r),g(r)) independent of z, write B=Bz​z+∇×(Az). Ideal induction becomes
(∂t​+f∂ϕ​)A=0,(∂t​+f∂ϕ​)Bz​=rg′​∂ϕ​A.
(17)
The first equation expresses magnetic flux freezing of the transverse flux function, while the second is axial stretching Br​g′. Starting from a uniform field B0​x gives A(r,ϕ,t)=B0​rsin(ϕ−f(r)t) and Bz​(r,ϕ,t)=B0​tg′(r)cos(ϕ−f(r)t). In complex azimuthal-mode notation, A=B0​re−ift and Bz​=iB0​tg′e−ift, obtained by elementary integrating factors. The transverse field has Br​=r−1Aϕ​ and Bϕ​=−Ar​, preserving zero divergence.

Cartesian magnetic flux function (ψ)

Words: 147 Articles: 2
Ideal magnetohydrodynamic induction equation OurBigBook.com
For a y-independent solenoidal magnetic field, the transverse components can be written Bx​=−ψz​ and Bz​=ψx​. Contours of ψ are transverse magnetic field lines. The independent axial component By​ can twist the flux tube. Under the MHD induction equation, an additive time-dependent gauge can be chosen so that Dψ/Dt=0.

Magnetic island

Words: 56
Cartesian magnetic flux function OurBigBook.com
A magnetic island in a planar magnetic field is a region of closed magnetic field lines surrounding an extremum of the Cartesian magnetic flux function. A surrounding separatrix can pass through a saddle of that function and separate the island from other flux regions. In ideal incompressible flow, the flux-function value carried by each fluid particle and the area enclosed by each material contour are conserved.

Cartesian magnetostatic flux-function equilibrium

Words: 46
Cartesian magnetic flux function OurBigBook.com
In a y-independent magnetostatic equilibrium with no axial pressure or gravitational force, ∇ψ×∇By​=0. Thus By​=b(ψ) on a regular connected flux region. The remaining balance is [∇2ψ+bb′]∇ψ/μ0​+∇p+ρ∇Φ=0. Constancy on separate components of a level set does not automatically give one global single-valued b.

Axisymmetric magnetic winding (∂t​Bϕ​=RBp​⋅∇Ω)

Words: 132 Articles: 2
Ideal magnetohydrodynamic induction equation OurBigBook.com
For prescribed axisymmetric differential rotation u=RΩeϕ​, the ideal magnetohydrodynamic induction equation and Gauss's law for magnetism give
∂t​Bp​=0,∂t​Bϕ​=RBp​⋅∇Ω.
(18)
The poloidal field is unchanged while rotational shear generates a toroidal magnetic field. For time-independent Ω, the toroidal component grows linearly until neglected dynamical feedback becomes relevant.

Magnetic-pressure equality radius under Keplerian winding (Req​∝t2/3)

Words: 70
Axisymmetric magnetic winding OurBigBook.com
For Keplerian rotation, initial BR​∝R−1 and thermal pressure p∝R−2, axisymmetric magnetic winding gives Bϕ​=−(3/2)ΩtBR​. If the initial plasma beta is βp​>1, the formal equality of magnetic pressure and gas pressure occurs at
Req3​=4(βp​−1)9GMt2​.
(19)
The magnetic-to-thermal pressure ratio decreases with radius, so magnetic pressure dominates inside this radius. In a disk with a finite radial range, an equality radius exists in the disk only when this formal radius lies within that range.

Ferraro's law of isorotation (Bp​⋅∇Ω=0)

Words: 23
Axisymmetric magnetic winding OurBigBook.com
A stationary axisymmetric magnetic field in ideal purely rotational flow requires constant angular velocity along the magnetic field lines of its poloidal magnetic field. Otherwise axisymmetric magnetic winding generates a time-dependent toroidal component.

Entropy advection equation

Words: 26
Ideal magnetohydrodynamics OurBigBook.com
For an adiabatic ideal fluid, entropy is materially conserved away from shocks: Ds/Dt=0. For a perfect gas this is equivalent to Dp/Dt+γp∇⋅u=0.

Magnetohydrodynamic shock (MHD shock)

Words: 307 Articles: 6
Ideal magnetohydrodynamics OurBigBook.com
A magnetohydrodynamic shock is a discontinuity satisfying conservation of mass, momentum, energy, normal magnetic field, and tangential electric field.

Perpendicular magnetohydrodynamic shock (B2​/B1​=ρ2​/ρ1​)

Words: 130 Articles: 1
Magnetohydrodynamic shock OurBigBook.com
For a planar magnetohydrodynamic shock with normal velocity and tangential magnetic field, mass conservation gives ρu=m and the ideal magnetohydrodynamic induction equation gives uB constant across the front. Hence B/ρ is unchanged, expressing magnetic flux freezing. Normal momentum flux is ρu2+p+B2/(2μ0​), and energy flux per unit mass flux is u2/2+γp/[(γ−1)ρ]+B2/(μ0​ρ), apart from a smooth common gravitational potential. The amplified tangential field contributes both magnetic pressure and magnetic energy transport.

Compression ratio of a perpendicular magnetohydrodynamic shock (x=ρ2​/ρ1​)

Words: 74
Perpendicular magnetohydrodynamic shock OurBigBook.com
Put c12​=γp1​/ρ1​ and vA12​=B12​/(μ0​ρ1​). The mass, momentum and energy jump conditions for a perpendicular magnetohydrodynamic shock factor into the unchanged state x=1 and
(2−γ)vA12​x2+[(γ−1)u12​+2c12​+γvA12​]x−(γ+1)u12​=0.
(20)
For the compressive physical branch x>1, positive downstream pressure implies x<(γ+1)/(γ−1) when γ>1 and the upstream sound speed or Alfvén speed is nonzero. Indeed the polynomial implies
ρ1​p2​​=(γ+1)−(γ−1)xc12​[(γ+1)x−(γ−1)]/γ+(γ−1)vA12​(x−1)3/2​.
(21)
It then gives u12​>c12​+vA12​: the upstream flow exceeds the perpendicular fast magnetosonic wave speed. The exactly cold unmagnetized strong-shock limit reaches the upper compression bound.

Parallel magnetohydrodynamic shock

Words: 62
Magnetohydrodynamic shock OurBigBook.com
In a planar magnetohydrodynamic shock with both velocity and magnetic field normal to the front, the normal magnetic field is continuous. Its normal Maxwell stress tensor contribution is consequently the same on both sides, and the Poynting vector vanishes because u×B=0. The remaining jump conditions are the ordinary Rankine-Hugoniot conditions for a perfect gas. This is the purely parallel branch; an oblique or switch-on shock has additional transverse fields and is not covered by this reduction.

Ideal magnetohydrodynamic shock conditions (ideal MHD shock conditions)

Words: 39
Magnetohydrodynamic shock OurBigBook.com
The ideal magnetohydrodynamic shock conditions are the Rankine-Hugoniot jump conditions for mass, momentum, energy, and magnetic flux. For a dynamically weak magnetic field, the normal field is continuous while the tangential field is multiplied by the gas compression ratio.

de Hoffmann–Teller frame

Words: 31
Magnetohydrodynamic shock OurBigBook.com
The de Hoffmann-Teller frame is a tangentially boosted shock frame in which the electric field vanishes. Ideal MHD then makes the fluid velocity parallel to the magnetic field on both sides.

Rotational discontinuity in magnetohydrodynamics

Words: 26
Magnetohydrodynamic shock OurBigBook.com
A rotational discontinuity changes the tangential direction of the magnetic field and velocity while leaving density, pressure, and normal components continuous. The normal flow is Alfvénic.

Axisymmetric magnetostatic Grad-Shafranov system

Words: 35
Ideal magnetohydrodynamics OurBigBook.com
For an axisymmetric vector potential A=∇α×∇ϕ+β∇ϕ, define
L=−r∂r​(r−1∂r​)−∂z2​.
(22)
Magnetostatic azimuthal force balance gives Lα=F(β). In a barotropic equilibrium the remaining balance integrates to
Lβ=F(β)F′(β)+r2ρG(β)
(23)
for flux functions F and G.

Axisymmetric magnetohydrodynamic wind (axisymmetric MHD wind)

Words: 1k Articles: 23
Ideal magnetohydrodynamics OurBigBook.com
A steady axisymmetric magnetohydrodynamic wind follows nested magnetic-flux surfaces and has conserved mass loading, field-line angular velocity, angular momentum, entropy, and Bernoulli quantities along each surface.

Cold radial magnetohydrodynamic wind integral (f(x,y)=constant)

Words: 88
Axisymmetric magnetohydrodynamic wind OurBigBook.com
For a cold equatorial axisymmetric magnetohydrodynamic wind with Bp​=CR−2 in the gravity of a point mass M, smooth crossing of the Alfvén surface gives ρa​=μ0​k2 and ℓ=ωRa2​. Put x=R/Ra​, y=ρ/ρa​, α=ω2Ra3​/(GM) and β=C2/(μ0​ρa​GMRa3​). The corotating energy, scaled by GM/Ra​, is
f=2α​[(y−1)2(x−x−1)2​−x2]+2x4y2β​−x1​.
(24)
The azimuthal velocity relative to field-line rotation is ωRa​(x−x−1)/(y−1) and the poloidal speed is C/(μ0​ρa​​Ra2​x2y). The apparent singularity at x=y=1 is interpreted through a smooth limiting slope. A nondegenerate magnetosonic crossing on a constant-f curve requires fx​=fy​=0 and a real admissible tangent slope.

Sub-Alfvénic isorotation in a steady axisymmetric wind (Ω≃ΩF​(MAp2​≪1))

Words: 102
Axisymmetric magnetohydrodynamic wind OurBigBook.com
Assume zero toroidal loop voltage in smooth steady ideal magnetohydrodynamics, so the poloidal flow aligns with the poloidal magnetic field. Write ρup​=ηBp​. The continuity equation makes η constant along a magnetic line. The induction equation gives the conserved field-line angular velocity ΩF​=Ω−ηBϕ​/(ρR). The azimuthal momentum equation is ρup​⋅∇(R2Ω)=Bp​⋅∇(RBϕ​)/μ0​; hence L=R2Ω−RBϕ​/(μ0​η) is also constant along the line.
With MAp2​=μ0​η2/ρ=∣up​∣2/vAp2​, eliminating Bϕ​ gives
Ω=1−MAp2​ΩF​−MAp2​L/R2​.
(25)
For MAp2​≪1 and nonsingular invariants, Ω=ΩF​+O(MAp2​) and matter approximately corotates along a field line. With exactly zero poloidal flow, induction directly gives Ferraro's law of isorotation. The approximation requires the correction MAp2​(ΩF​−L/R2) to be small on the segment in question.

Corotating energy invariant of an axisymmetric magnetic wind (ϵJ​=∣u∣2/2+Φ−ωRuϕ​)

Words: 46
Axisymmetric magnetohydrodynamic wind OurBigBook.com
For a pressure-free flowing poloidal flux surface, subtracting its angular velocity times the azimuthal momentum equation from the mechanical energy equation shows that ϵJ​ is constant. It equals poloidal kinetic energy plus (uϕ​−Rω)2/2+Φ−R2ω2/2. This is the total magnetohydrodynamic Bernoulli invariant minus ω times the total magnetohydrodynamic angular-momentum invariant, not the total energy alone.

Field-line angular velocity of an axisymmetric wind (u=kB/ρ+Rω(ψ)eϕ​)

Words: 37
Axisymmetric magnetohydrodynamic wind OurBigBook.com
In steady axisymmetric ideal magnetohydrodynamics, induction makes ω constant on regular connected poloidal flux surfaces. It describes field-line rotation. The material angular velocity is uϕ​/R=ω+kBϕ​/(ρR) and differs when the toroidal magnetic field contributes. If the poloidal magnetic field vanishes, the flux-surface integration requires separate treatment.

Poloidal magnetic flux function (ψ)

Words: 145 Articles: 3
Axisymmetric magnetohydrodynamic wind OurBigBook.com
For Bp​=∇ψ×∇ϕ, surfaces ψ=constant are poloidal magnetic surfaces and 2πψ is magnetic flux up to the choice of axial reference value.

Material advection of an axisymmetric magnetic flux function (DΨ/Dt=0)

Words: 41
Poloidal magnetic flux function OurBigBook.com
For an axisymmetric poloidal magnetic field Bp​=∇Ψ×∇ϕ, the ideal magnetohydrodynamic induction equation gives ∂t​Ψ+up​⋅∇Ψ=0, after fixing the time-dependent additive constant in Ψ. A regular axial reference makes 2πΨ the enclosed magnetic flux. This scalar statement of magnetic flux freezing holds even when rotation also produces a toroidal magnetic field.

Axisymmetric magnetic flux surface (ψ=constant)

Words: 47
Poloidal magnetic flux function OurBigBook.com
A regular level surface of the axisymmetric poloidal magnetic flux function contains both the poloidal and toroidal magnetic field directions. Conservation along field lines can be expressed locally as a function of the flux label on connected regular surfaces. Degenerate points with no poloidal magnetic field and disconnected branches with the same label require separate treatment.

Power-law poloidal field near a disk surface

Words: 34
Poloidal magnetic flux function OurBigBook.com
If Ψ(R,0)=Ψ1​+Ψ0​(R/R0​)δ and the surface inclination to the vertical is a radius-independent α, then Bz​=δΨ0​Rδ−2/R0δ​ and BR​=Bz​tanα. The solenoidal vector field condition gives
∂z​Bz​∣0​=−Rδ−1​Bz​(R,0)tanα.
(26)
The constant offset in the poloidal magnetic flux function has no effect on the magnetic field.

Magnetohydrodynamic mass loading (k(ψ))

Words: 69 Articles: 1
Axisymmetric magnetohydrodynamic wind OurBigBook.com
When ρup​=kBp​, the flux-surface function k is the mass flux per unit poloidal magnetic flux.

Regular-axis alignment of steady poloidal ideal flow (ρu=k(ψ)B)

Words: 51
Magnetohydrodynamic mass loading OurBigBook.com
For steady axisymmetric ideal flow with only poloidal components, induction implies u×B=Ceϕ​/R. Axis regularity, or zero toroidal electromotive force, sets C=0. Continuity then gives ρu=k(ψ)B, locally on connected magnetic surfaces of the poloidal magnetic flux function. Without the zero-circulation condition, annular domains can support steady cross-field flow.

Field-line angular velocity (ω(ψ))

Words: 20
Axisymmetric magnetohydrodynamic wind OurBigBook.com
Ideal induction in a steady axisymmetric flow makes each magnetic surface rotate with a constant field-line angular velocity ω(ψ).

Magnetohydrodynamic angular-momentum invariant (ℓ(ψ))

Words: 91 Articles: 1
Axisymmetric magnetohydrodynamic wind OurBigBook.com
The total specific angular momentum transported by matter and magnetic stress is
ℓ=ruϕ​−μ0​krBϕ​​,
(27)
and is constant on each magnetic surface.

Maxwell torque conservation in an axisymmetric wind (FJ​=ρup​suϕ​−μ0−1​Bp​sBϕ​)

Words: 71
Magnetohydrodynamic angular-momentum invariant OurBigBook.com
In a steady axisymmetric magnetohydrodynamic wind, axisymmetric pressure and Newtonian gravity exert no azimuthal torque. The azimuthal momentum equation is ρup​⋅∇(suϕ​)=μ0−1​Bp​⋅∇(sBϕ​). Mass conservation and the solenoidal vector field condition imply ∇⋅FJ​=0. With magnetohydrodynamic mass loading ρup​=κBp​, the transported angular momentum per unit poloidal magnetic flux is ℓ=κsuϕ​−sBϕ​/μ0​. It is constant on connected regular poloidal flux surfaces. The usual specific magnetohydrodynamic angular-momentum invariant is L=ℓ/κ, provided κ=0; confusing these two normalizations loses a factor of mass loading in the wind torque.

Magnetohydrodynamic Bernoulli invariant (ϵ(ψ))

Words: 68 Articles: 1
Axisymmetric magnetohydrodynamic wind OurBigBook.com
Along a steady axisymmetric ideal-MHD wind, the total specific energy
ϵ=21​∣u∣2+Φ+h−μ0​krωBϕ​​
(28)
is constant on each magnetic surface. The last term is the electromagnetic energy transported per unit mass flux.

Isothermal magnetic Bernoulli integral (ϵ(ψ))

Words: 36
Magnetohydrodynamic Bernoulli invariant OurBigBook.com
In aligned steady ideal flow with p=cs2​ρ and constant isothermal sound speed, the Lorentz force density has no field-parallel component. Projecting momentum along the magnetic field makes u2/2+Φ+cs2​ln(ρ/ρ0​) constant on each connected magnetic surface. The arbitrary reference density changes only the additive constant.

Alfvén surface

Words: 126 Articles: 2
Axisymmetric magnetohydrodynamic wind OurBigBook.com
An Alfvén surface is where the poloidal flow speed equals the poloidal Alfvén speed. Smooth passage through it imposes a regularity condition relating field-line angular velocity and angular momentum.

Alfvén radius (RA​)

Words: 65
Alfvén surface OurBigBook.com
The Alfvén radius characterizes where a magnetized stellar wind crosses its Alfvén surface. For a roughly radial wind, vwind​≃B/μ0​ρ​ and M˙w​≃4πRA2​ρvwind​. The wind's angular-momentum lever arm is of order RA​: its torque is J˙∼−M˙w​ΩRA2​, up to geometry factors. The precise wind invariant uses the cylindrical radius of the surface crossing, rather than necessarily its spherical radius.

Alfvén-surface regularity condition for an axisymmetric wind

Words: 32
Alfvén surface OurBigBook.com
If rA​ is the cylindrical radius at which MA2​=μ0​k2/ρ=1, finite azimuthal velocity and magnetic field require
ℓ=ωrA2​.
(29)
This cancels the simultaneous numerator and denominator zeros in the wind's azimuthal integrals.

Asymptotic energy of a radial magnetohydrodynamic wind

Words: 28
Axisymmetric magnetohydrodynamic wind OurBigBook.com
If r2∣Bp​∣→F and up​→u∞​ along an open magnetic surface, then
Bϕ​∼−u∞​rωF​,∣vAϕ​∣→ωμ0​ku∞​F​​.
(30)
When enthalpy and gravity vanish asymptotically, the Bernoulli invariant becomes
ϵ=21​u∞2​+μ0​ku∞​ω2F​.
(31)

Magnetocentrifugal acceleration

Words: 195 Articles: 3
Axisymmetric magnetohydrodynamic wind OurBigBook.com
Magnetocentrifugal acceleration occurs when matter tied to a rotating inclined magnetic field moves outward under the effective centrifugal force. For a Keplerian disc, cold launching is possible when the field tilts by more than 30∘ from the vertical.

Thirty-degree magnetocentrifugal launching criterion (α>π/6)

Words: 95 Articles: 1
Magnetocentrifugal acceleration OurBigBook.com
For a cold corotating field line anchored in a circular point-mass orbit, the effective potential has meridional Hessian ω2diag(−3,1). Along a straight line inclined by α to the vertical its quadratic curvature is ω2(1−4sin2α). Negative curvature gives the strict local launching criterion. Equality is marginal and global escape requires additional information.
Marginal straight-line launch at thirty degrees (ΔΦeff​/(GM/R0​)=−7(s/R0​)3/16+O(s4))
Words: 44
Thirty-degree magnetocentrifugal launching criterion OurBigBook.com
At exactly thirty degrees the quadratic curvature vanishes, but the specified straight-line point-mass effective potential is downhill for small positive displacement at cubic order. Thus the strict negative-curvature criterion does not exclude every nonlinear one-sided marginal launch. An exactly stationary bead remains at equilibrium until displaced.

Magnetocentrifugal launching criterion in a flattened power-law potential (αcrit​=arctan(∣λ∣/β+2​))

Words: 62
Magnetocentrifugal acceleration OurBigBook.com
In a flattened power-law gravitational potential Φ=Φ0​R0β​(R2+λ2z2)−β/2, a magnetic surface corotating with its disk footpoint has an effective potential with meridional Hessian matrix Ωf2​diag[−(β+2),λ2] there. A cold outward displacement along a field inclined by α to the vertical is downhill when tan2α>λ2/(β+2). Equality is marginal and can depend on higher derivatives and field-line curvature; this is a local launching criterion, not a guarantee of a global escaping wind.
